automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.rule: Only public sources visibly published or updated inside this seven-day window are qualifying.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Backslash reported a Codex CLI exec-mode prompt-injection path where attacker-controlled instructions in repository AGENTS.md could run before the user's explicit task and could be used for credential exfiltration.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local request packages and durable instruction files need explicit trust boundaries, provenance checks, and approval rules for repo-local instructions before agents execute commands or access secrets.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should keep broad Codex vulnerability details upstream and update local practice only for trusted instruction boundaries, request package hygiene, and approval gates.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub added Codex as an agent provider in JetBrains IDEs and exposed agent customization surfaces for hooks, MCP server management, workspace-level MCP configuration, generated instruction and skill files, and approval settings for Copilot CLI sessions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: MCP governance and portable skill/runbook practice now need to assume agent customization files, workspace-level MCP manifests, and approval policy controls can be managed directly in developer tooling.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route product-release details upstream; keep local implications for MCP manifest review, generated customization file review, and approval-setting conventions.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub's June 2026 VS Code Copilot release notes include agent session organization so users can group related agent sessions and rearrange them in the Agents window.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local request packages and ownership rosters should treat agent sessions as durable work containers that may need naming, grouping, ownership, and handoff conventions.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest as a local operating-model note only if agent-session organization changes how teams name, hand off, or audit work packages.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Explainx published a developer skills roadmap that sequences structured prompting, agentic coding tools, MCP, agents, RAG, and fine-tuning, arguing that teams often plateau when training stops at autocomplete.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The selected learning-path and tier-convention leaves can use this as a current public signal for sequencing skills before giving developers broader tool, MCP, RAG, or autonomous-agent responsibility.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Prefer local practice synthesis around training progression; route broad MCP or RAG background upstream.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: ITPro reported Gartner analysis that agentic systems can bypass traditional interface-heavy SaaS workflows, expose up to 234 billion dollars in application spending to agentic arbitrage by 2030, and push vendors toward outcome-based value and cross-domain workflows.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local adoption agreements and economics guidance should distinguish seat-based tool rollout from outcome-based agent workflows that capture customer context and automate across systems.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep broad SaaS-market analysis upstream; local ingest should focus on economics criteria for adopting, funding, and pruning agent workflows.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar argued that enterprise agent adoption is moving toward agent frameworks wrapped by infrastructure, guardrails, and policy enforcement because unconstrained autonomous agents create unacceptable operational risk.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Ownership rosters, approval boundaries, and operating agreements should make guardrails and policy enforcement part of the agent operating model rather than optional tooling around a model.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route named product and ecosystem claims upstream; keep only local guardrail, policy, and accountability implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Business Insider reported Jensen Huang's statement that Nvidia software engineers increasingly prefer building agents over writing Python code and now work on agents, benchmarks, and guardrails.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local team-design leaves should treat agent building, benchmark design, and guardrail work as core engineering responsibilities, especially for senior-led teams and junior learning paths.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route Nvidia background upstream; local ingest can update workforce-practice framing around agents, benchmarks, and guardrails as engineering work.

excluded_candidates.reason: Search result and page indicate roughly three weeks old, outside the seven-day cutoff.
